title: 3 AI-Related Stocks Worth a Closer Look After Pullbacks
author: Na
description: Three AI infrastructure stocks—Vertiv, Applied Optoelectronics, and Innodata—have experienced significant pullbacks from their 2026 highs despite maintaining strong underlying growth fundamentals. Each company offers exposure to different segments of AI infrastructure: power/cooling systems, optical networking, and data services. Their recent earnings remain solid with robust growth outlooks, suggesting potential opportunities for investors.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong fundamentals with 24% YoY sales growth, 60% EPS jump, and raised full-year guidance expecting 30-32% organic growth. Pullback from highs creates attractive entry point despite solid underlying demand for data center infrastructure.

Exceptional growth with 86% YoY revenue increase, fifth consecutive quarterly record, and 140% data center revenue jump. Management expects demand to exceed production capacity through mid-2027. Sharp pullback from peak makes valuation more attractive.

Record quarterly revenue up 58% YoY with 92% EBITDA growth and improved customer diversification. Management maintains 40% revenue growth guidance for 2026. Significant pullback from highs presents opportunity despite strong execution.

title: Eaton to Boost U.S. Power Capacity With $242M Arkansas Plant
author: Na
description: Eaton Corporation plans to invest over $242 million in a new one-million-square-foot manufacturing facility in North Little Rock, Arkansas to double U.S. Fibrebond capacity and create 1,200 jobs. The expansion supports strong demand in critical-power infrastructure, with Electrical Americas reporting 18% organic sales growth, 41% order growth, and 33% backlog growth in Q2 2026. The facility will help address capacity constraints and deepen exposure to AI infrastructure and grid modernization.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong organic sales growth (18%), significant order increases (41%), growing backlog (33%), major capital investment ($242M) to expand capacity, raised 2026 guidance to 11-13%, and strategic positioning in high-growth AI infrastructure and grid modernization markets.
Mentioned as a peer company planning similar manufacturing expansion in Wisconsin, but no specific performance metrics or strategic details provided to indicate positive or negative sentiment.

title: Every Hyperscaler Raised Capex Again. These 3 Boring Industrials Get Paid No Matter Who Wins the AI Race.
author: Patrick Sanders
description: Major tech companies (Alphabet, Amazon, Meta) are significantly increasing capital expenditures for AI infrastructure. Rather than betting on which tech company will succeed, investors can gain exposure to the AI boom through industrial companies that supply essential infrastructure—power generation, electrical systems, and cooling hardware—regardless of which tech platform dominates.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong revenue growth (24% YoY) with power generation segment up 72% due to data center demand. Stock up 91% in past 12 months. Positioned as key AI infrastructure supplier with natural gas generators for data centers.

Provides essential power distribution and circuit protection for data centers. Revenue growth of 21% YoY ($8.53B vs $7.02B). Benefits from increasing power demands as AI clusters now consume up to 500 MW. Stock up 13% in past year.

Specialized power and cooling hardware for data centers with custom solutions for Nvidia's Vera Rubin architecture. Revenue up 24% YoY to $3.27B with net income up 54%. Stock up 115% in past year, indicating strong market recognition.

title: 3 Millionaire-Maker Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks to Buy Now
author: Micah Zimmerman
description: The article highlights three AI infrastructure stocks—Astera Labs, Credo Technology, and Vertiv—that address critical bottlenecks in AI data center scaling. Astera Labs specializes in connectivity solutions with 93% YoY revenue growth and a $6.5B Amazon warrant agreement. Credo Technology manufactures active electrical cables with 272% YoY growth but faces customer concentration risks. Vertiv dominates power and cooling systems with a $15B backlog and strong positioning in liquid cooling demand.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong 93% YoY revenue growth, high 76.3% gross margins indicating design-focused business model, Scorpio product family expected to become largest product line, and strategic $6.5B warrant agreement with Amazon provide significant growth catalysts and validation.

Exceptional 272% YoY revenue growth with guidance above 200% for full-year, steep adoption curve for active electrical cables, and expanding product portfolio (ZeroFlap Optics, OmniConnect gearboxes). However, sentiment is tempered by significant customer concentration risk and high stock volatility.

Massive $15B backlog with 2.9 book-to-bill ratio indicating strong demand, binding purchase orders with advance payments, and strategic positioning in liquid cooling where lead times have extended significantly. Expanding manufacturing capacity by 40-50% demonstrates confidence in sustained demand.

Mentioned as a strategic partner through Astera Labs' $6.5B warrant agreement, indicating Amazon's commitment to AI infrastructure scaling, but no direct investment recommendation or analysis provided.

title: Vertiv Just Made an Up to $2.6 Billion Bet to Solve AI Data Centers' Biggest Bottleneck
author: Matt Dilallo
description: Vertiv is acquiring Utility Innovations for up to $2.6 billion to address the power supply bottleneck in AI data centers. The deal extends Vertiv's capabilities across the full power value chain from grid to chip, including microgrid solutions and on-site generation, enabling faster time-to-power for data center developers.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strategic acquisition expands capabilities to solve critical AI data center bottleneck; expected to be accretive to earnings in first year; positions company across full power value chain; supports continued robust growth trajectory with 31% sales growth and 72% EPS surge expected

Highlighted as beneficiary of accelerating demand for on-site power solutions; demonstrated rapid deployment capability (55 days vs. 90-day target); expected 100% revenue growth in 2026; partnership expansion with Oracle validates market opportunity
